questions.q: Why does validate_billing_load run as its own separate task before load_billing?
options: So a malformed export fails at the very first task with a specific signal, instead of loading bad data or failing confusingly later
Because Airflow requires every DAG to start with a validation task
Because SnowflakeOperator cannot run COPY INTO without a prior validation step
To make the DAG diagram look more complete
questions.explain: Validating first catches a malformed file at the earliest possible point, with a clear, specific failure signal rather than a confusing downstream error.

questions.q: Why must both load_billing and load_usage succeed before dbt_run starts?
options: load_billing and load_usage must run sequentially, never in parallel
Airflow requires exactly two upstream tasks before any BashOperator can run
dbt cannot run unless usage_events table is empty
int_subscriber_activity joins billing and usage data together -- running dbt against only half the day's raw data would produce quietly wrong numbers, not an error
questions.explain: A join against incomplete raw data wouldn't error -- it would silently produce an incorrect result, which is exactly the failure mode this dependency ordering prevents.

questions.q: Why are dbt_run and dbt_test separate tasks instead of one combined step?
options: So Airflow's task-level status distinguishes "models built but a test caught a real data problem" from "the dbt run itself broke" -- a materially different, more actionable failure signal
This is a stylistic choice with no functional difference
dbt does not support running tests and models in the same command under any circumstances
Separate tasks run faster than combined ones
questions.explain: Separating these tasks makes the specific failure type visible at a glance in Airflow's UI -- the same pattern the Airflow course's own Airflow + dbt lesson teaches.

questions.q: Why do load_billing and load_usage run in parallel rather than sequentially?
options: Neither task depends on the other's output, so there's no reason to force them to wait on each other
Snowflake requires all COPY INTO statements to run simultaneously
Parallel execution is required by Airflow's scheduler
Sequential execution would cause a SQL syntax error
questions.explain: They load into two separate, independent raw tables -- running them in parallel is simply faster with no correctness downside, since neither reads the other's output.

questions.q: What does the `>>` operator do in this DAG's final line?
options: Declares the task dependency order -- each task (or list of tasks) only runs after the one(s) before it succeed
Comments out the line for debugging purposes
Runs all listed tasks simultaneously with no ordering
Pipes the SQL output of one task directly into the next task's input
questions.explain: `>>` is Airflow's dependency-declaration operator -- it establishes the order tasks must complete in, which is what makes this a real orchestrated sequence rather than independent tasks.
